correctness.rationale: For arbitrary finite quiver including loops and repeated arrows, q=p^f finite and k>=1, units of F_q Q/J^2 are diagonal nonzero entries plus independent arrow coordinates. kth power on arrow s->t is x_e times C_k(d_s,d_t)=sum_{j=0}^{k-1}d_s^(k-1-j)d_t^j, a divided difference with C_k(a,a)=k a^(k-1). If p|k, every arrow with equal target diagonals is forced zero, yielding h^n q^{m_=(u)} roots under stated compatibility. If p does not divide k, within equal target diagonal classes the prescribed nonzero arrows impose equal endpoint root labels and zero arrows with different labels contribute q independent arrow choices, giving weighted constrained colorings. Off-class arrows contribute one choice. Consequently image sizes q^m r^n vs Z_Q(r,q) and identity root counts Z_Q(h,q) vs h^n q^m; product expansion by q+(1-q)1_same gives Fortuin-Kasteleyn-type formula. Element orders via Mobius inversion and exponent p(q-1) when m>0 follow from torus and arrow subgroup. Independently enumerated 8,694 target/k finite cases over GF(2),GF(3),GF(5). Infinite claim established by coordinate proof, not enumeration.
residual_risks: The independent finite checks are bounded and do not themselves establish infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: All-fiber distributions and power-image sizes across the characteristic transition are natural invariants of finite algebraic groups. The precise root multiplicity in a general unit group is not merely an exponent observation; the quiver graph-colored partition formulation systematically handles loops, repeated arrows, arbitrary finite fields and every exponent. This is a complete natural family classification with element-order consequences.
residual_risks: Value concerns the precisely stated natural object and invariant; the finding does not settle unclaimed broader classifications.
